title: Closest delivery drops
prompt:
A drone at the origin (0, 0) can serve k drop points; return the k points closest to it by straight-line distance.

- points: 1 to 50,000 pairs [x, y] of integers between -10^4 and 10^4; duplicates may appear and each counts separately. 1 <= k <= len(points).
- Order the result by distance ascending, then by x ascending, then by y ascending (compare x*x + y*y to avoid square roots).
- Return a list of k [x, y] pairs in that order.
hints: Sorting all points works but does more than needed when k is much smaller than n.
Keep the k best points seen so far in a max-heap keyed by (distance squared, x, y); its root is the worst of them.
For each point, push it and pop the root if the heap holds more than k. At the end pop everything (worst first) and reverse.

solution.explanation: A max-heap of size k holds the best k candidates with the worst one on top, so each new point either replaces that worst candidate or is discarded. Comparing squared distances keeps everything in exact integers, and the (distance, x, y) key makes ties deterministic. heapq.nsmallest does the same bounded selection and returns the k items sorted.

complexity.notes: Quickselect finds the k nearest in O(n) average time, but the result still needs an O(k log k) sort for the required order.

followUps: Points stream in forever and you must answer the current k nearest at any moment. What would you keep?
